Grateful for the opportunity to attend the announcement for the University of Kentucky Markey Cancer Center’s National Cancer Institute designation as a Comprehensive Care Canter. 

Promoting access to quality healthcare has been one of my top priorities in Congress, and I am thrilled to have such a distinguished cancer research and treatment center in Central Kentucky.

On Friday, I presented $350,000 from the Fiscal Year 2023 Community Project Funding process to Saint Joseph Berea Hospital. 

This funding will be used to purchase a cardiac focused nuclear medicine camera with multiple components of advanced technology. This funding is vital to enhancing healthcare accessibility and quality in Central Kentucky, ensuring that Saint Joseph Berea remains at the forefront of medical excellence and patient care.

Thank you Big I Kentucky for the invitation to speak at your annual convention in Louisville. 

Insurance agents play an integral role in communities across the Commonwealth and I appreciate the work that they do. https://t.co/0lYSoYvgpD

I enjoyed the opportunity to welcome George Ridings from Richmond to my Washington, DC office. 

George and I were able to discuss legislative priorities for insurance agents and financial advisors following NAIFA leadership meetings. Thank you to Ridings Insurance for assisting Kentuckians with financial planning, asset protection, and wealth management.

The Thrive Center at Baptist Health Richmond is providing much needed inpatient behavioral health services in Madison and surrounding counties. I was happy to assist the Thrive Center in securing $390,000 in federal funding to expand their outpatient behavioral health services. Thank you to the Thrive Center and Baptist Health Richmond providers who continue to ensure our communities have access to top quality mental health services.

I am thankful to hear that my friend, @SteveScalise, is in complete remission and will be returning to Washington next week. His resilience and determination throughout his treatment are a testament to his strength. Welcome back, Leader Scalise!

Great to meet with Kentucky SHAPE to discuss health and physical education priorities. It is imperative that we prepare, train, recruit and retain formative educators in our elementary and secondary schools.

The Biden Admin strikes again, weaponizing the CFPB to push their belief that debts don't need to be repaid and buy votes in the upcoming election. Today's proposal to ban medical debt info from credit reports is reckless, putting businesses on the hook and increasing risks in our financial system.

June is Alzheimer's and Brain Awareness Month, a time to focus on the millions of families affected by these diseases. I'm proud to support the NAPA Reauthorization Act and the BOLD Act. These crucial bills enhance care, support families, and bolster public health efforts to combat Alzheimer’s. Together, we can work towards a future free from these devastating illnesses.

I enjoyed the opportunity to visit the new site where Lexington Rescue Mission, Jubilee Jobs, and Isaiah House’s Community Health Center will soon come together under one roof. It is great to see these amazing organizations collaborating to better serve our community! https://t.co/kfPnbepe4U

Had a fantastic day in Estill and Powell Counties, meeting with community leaders and healthcare providers. 

I provided updates on my work in Washington to the Estill County Chamber of Commerce and had the opportunity to meet with Estill Schools Superintendent Charlie Brock. I also visited the Foothills Community Health Center in Clay City, Mercy Health - Marcum and Wallace Hospital in Irvine, and Estill Medical Clinic. Thanks to everyone for your warm hospitality and dedication to our community!

I joined Chairman @PatrickMcHenry in sending a letter to CFPB Director Chopra, condemning the Bureau's latest overreach on medical debt. These unjustified actions threaten the accuracy and integrity of consumer credit reports, ultimately harming the very people the CFPB is supposed to protect.
